accuracy.evidence: Matches NC Y2: × as equal groups/arrays, ÷ as sharing/grouping, = as same value (equivalence), not only 'answer on the right'.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets ×-as-add, ÷-as-subtract, digit-sticking, operational equals, and swapping ×/÷ in predictions, mix step, challenge why(), and adult notes.

lab_distinct.evidence: Lab is symbol-meaning matching, array build, equal share, and equals-balance — not fact fluency (flagsum5) or number bonds (flagnbonds).

lab_teaches.evidence: Learner must match each sign, build 2×3, share 8÷4, balance 6=6, and pick ÷ for a sharing story before confirmation text.

predictions.evidence: Wrong options (take away for ×; stick digits; answer-on-the-right; × for sharing) are the slips later tasks overturn.

challenge_feedback.evidence: why() names add-for-×, sub-for-÷, stick, right-only equals, left-only, and mul/div swaps specifically.

readability.evidence: Ages 6–7 wording: short kid lines, concrete bags/plates/array language; curriculum terms defined in situ.

no_filler.evidence: No delve/journey phrasing; each line teaches a sign job, an array, a share, or an equals check.

mobile.evidence: Large lbtn controls; array drag and share drag work at phone width; challenge buttons stack.

accessibility.evidence: Match/array/share/equal/story steps expose lbtn twins for every canvas action; say() updates the canvas aria-label; challenge uses aria-live status.

sources: UK National Curriculum 2013 Mathematics Year 2: multiplication and division — equal groups, arrays, sharing; equals as equivalence
NCETM / DfE ready-to-progress: 2MD-1 recognise equal groups; understanding = as same value
